easy.def: A tool that makes your voice louder.
examples: The singer held the microphone.
I spoke into the microphone.
The microphone is on.

more.def: A device that picks up sound and sends it to speakers or a recorder.
examples: The speaker tapped the microphone to test it.
I spoke into the microphone at the assembly.
The microphone squealed.

easy.def: The center of something.
examples: Stand in the middle.
The middle of the cake is soft.
He sat in the middle.

more.def: The part that is in the center, with equal parts around it.
examples: A line runs down the middle of the road.
She sat in the middle of the back seat.
The middle of the pizza was still hot.

easy.def: In the center.
examples: The middle seat is mine.
She is the middle child.
The middle one is mine.

more.def: Located between two ends or sides.
examples: My middle brother plays the drums.
The middle shelf holds the books.
Take the middle path through the woods.

easy.def: Twelve o'clock at night.
examples: The clock struck midnight.
I was fast asleep at midnight.
We stayed up until midnight on New Year's Eve.

more.def: Twelve o'clock at night, when one day ends and the next begins.
examples: The old clock chimed twelve times at midnight.
The campers watched the stars at midnight.
At midnight the date on the calendar changes.

easy.def: Very strong.
examples: The mighty lion roared.
He is a mighty giant.
A mighty wind blew.

more.def: Very strong and powerful.
examples: The mighty river carried boats to the sea.
The knight swung his mighty sword in the old tale.
A mighty oak tree stood at the edge of the field.

easy.def: To move to a new place when the season changes.
examples: Some birds migrate when it gets cold.
Whales migrate to warm water.
The geese migrate in the fall.

more.def: To travel from one place to another at certain times of year, as many animals do.
examples: Monarch butterflies migrate thousands of miles to warmer places each fall.
Huge herds of zebras migrate to find fresh grass.
Some whales migrate thousands of miles every year.

easy.def: A long distance.
examples: We walked a mile.
The school is one mile away.
He ran a mile.

more.def: A unit for measuring distance, equal to 5,280 feet.
examples: The path around the lake is two miles long.
We hiked one mile before lunch.
A mile is about as long as seventeen football fields.

easy.def: About soldiers and armies.
examples: A military base.
He wore a military uniform.
The military band marched.

more.def: Having to do with soldiers, armies or war.
examples: The military band played in the parade.
Soldiers lined up in a military camp.
The military base is outside of town.

easy.def: A white drink that comes from cows.
examples: I drink milk.
Cows give milk.
The milk is cold.

more.def: A white liquid that comes from cows and other mammals, used as a drink and in food.
examples: I drink a glass of milk with breakfast.
Goat milk can be made into cheese.
The baby kitten drank its mother's milk.

easy.def: To get a drink from a cow.
examples: The farmer milks the cow.
She milks the goat.
He milked the cows.

more.def: To draw the white drink out of a cow or goat.
examples: The farmer milks the cows every morning.
She milked the goat before breakfast.
They milked the cow by hand.

easy.def: A building where grain is made into flour.
examples: The mill grinds wheat.
The old mill is by the river.
The mill has a wheel.

more.def: A building with machinery where grain is ground into flour, or where goods are made.
examples: The old mill ground wheat into flour.
A water wheel turned at the mill.
The mill stood beside the stream.

easy.def: A very big number: 1,000,000.
examples: A million stars are in the sky.
The city has a million people.
I wish I had a million toys.

more.def: The number 1,000,000, which is one thousand thousands.
examples: More than a million people live in the city.
The library has about a million books.
A million seconds is about eleven and a half days.

easy.def: A person who has a million dollars or more.
examples: The millionaire has a big house.
A millionaire gave money.
The millionaire is rich.

more.def: A very rich person who has at least a million dollars.
examples: The millionaire lived in a huge house.
A millionaire gave money to the hospital.
The millionaire bought a boat.

easy.def: The part of you that thinks and feels.
examples: Use your mind.
I changed my mind.
Keep it in mind.

more.def: The part of a person that thinks, remembers, and has ideas.
examples: A good puzzle gives your mind a workout.
She changed her mind and chose the blue one.
The song stayed in my mind all day.

easy.def: To be upset about something.
examples: I do not mind waiting.
Do you mind the noise?
She does not mind.

more.def: To be bothered or upset by something.
examples: I do not mind sharing my crayons with you.
Would you mind closing the window, please?
He minded the cold less than his brother did.

easy.def: A word for something that belongs to me.
examples: That book is mine.
The red cup is mine.
Is this one yours or mine?

more.def: A word used for something that belongs to the person who is speaking.
examples: I found a blue backpack, but it is not mine.
Your drawing is great, and mine is not as good.
The seat next to the window is mine.

easy.def: The least amount.
examples: The minimum age is five.
Use the minimum of salt.
The minimum score is ten.

more.def: The smallest amount or number that is allowed or possible.
examples: The minimum age for the ride is five.
Add the minimum amount of water.
The test has a minimum of ten questions.

easy.def: A leader of a church.
examples: The minister gave a talk.
The minister said a prayer.
The minister greeted us.

more.def: A person who leads religious services in some churches.
examples: The minister gave a talk on Sunday morning.
The minister greeted everyone at the church door.
A minister led the prayers.

easy.def: A leader in some governments.
examples: She is a minister in the government.
The prime minister gave a speech.
He is the minister of education.

more.def: A person who is in charge of a part of a government.
examples: The minister of health spoke on the news.
The prime minister met other leaders.
She became the minister of education.

easy.def: Small and not important.
examples: It was a minor mistake.
The cut is minor.
A minor problem.

more.def: Small, or less important than other things.
examples: It was only a minor mistake.
The cut was minor and healed fast.
There were a few minor changes in the plan.

easy.def: A plant with a fresh, cool taste.
examples: The mint is green.
I put mint in my tea.
The mint smells nice.

more.def: A plant with a cool, fresh taste and smell that is used to flavor food.
examples: I put fresh mint in my tea.
The mint grew wild in the garden.
The gum tastes like mint.

easy.def: A sweet candy with a cool taste.
examples: I ate a mint.
The mint is white.
I sucked on a mint.

more.def: A small, sweet candy that has a cool, fresh flavor.
examples: I ate a mint after dinner.
The waiter left a mint with the bill.
She sucked on a mint.

easy.def: Take away.
examples: Five minus two is three.
Ten minus four is six.
Seven minus one is six.

more.def: Used in math to show that one number is taken from another.
examples: Twelve minus five is seven.
Ten minus four equals six.
I subtracted and found that nine minus three is six.

easy.def: Sixty seconds of time.
examples: Wait one minute.
It takes a minute.
I will be there in a minute.

more.def: A short period of time that is sixty seconds, or one sixtieth of an hour.
examples: An hour has sixty minutes.
Please wait a minute while I find my coat.
The bus will come in about ten minutes.

easy.def: Something wonderful that seems impossible.
examples: It was a miracle.
The rescue was a miracle.
A miracle happened.

more.def: A wonderful event that seems impossible or that cannot be explained.
examples: It was a miracle that no one was hurt.
The rescue of the lost puppy felt like a miracle.
Doctors called her recovery a miracle.

easy.def: A glass you look into to see yourself.
examples: I brush my hair in the mirror.
The mirror is on the wall.
She made a funny face in the mirror.

more.def: A smooth, shiny piece of glass that shows a picture of whatever is in front of it.
examples: A driver checks the mirror before changing lanes.
The dancers watched their moves in the huge mirror.
Light bounces off a mirror and lights up the dark corner.

easy.def: Silly things that can cause a little trouble.
examples: The puppy got into mischief.
My kitten is full of mischief.
The kids got into mischief in the mud.

more.def: Playful behavior that causes trouble or annoys people.
examples: The twins were always up to some kind of mischief.
The monkey's mischief made the zookeeper laugh.
There was a look of mischief in her eyes.

easy.def: Very unhappy.
examples: I felt miserable with a cold.
The rain made us miserable.
He felt miserable.

more.def: Very unhappy or uncomfortable.
examples: The cold, rainy day made us miserable.
I felt miserable with a stuffy nose.
The miserable puppy shivered in the rain.

easy.def: Great unhappiness.
examples: The rain caused misery.
He was in misery.
The misery ended.

more.def: A state of great sadness or pain.
examples: The cold rain made the camping trip a misery.
She was in misery with a bad cold.
The kitten's misery ended when we found it.

easy.def: To feel sad that someone is not here.
examples: I miss my friend.
She misses her mom.
We miss the old house.

more.def: To feel sad because someone or something is not with you.
examples: I miss my cousins when they go home after the holidays.
He missed his dog while he was at camp.
The children miss summer when winter comes.

easy.def: To not catch, hit, or get something.
examples: I miss the ball.
She missed the bus.
He missed a day of school.

more.def: To fail to hit, catch, reach, or be present for something.
examples: I missed the bus, so my dad drove me to school.
The player missed the ball and ran to get it.
Do not miss the show about space tonight.

easy.def: A rocket that can be aimed at something far away.
examples: The museum has an old missile.
The rocket looks like a missile.
The scientist studied the missile.

more.def: A flying weapon or rocket that is aimed at a faraway target.
examples: The museum has an old missile on display.
Scientists have developed missiles that can fly very far.
The missile was shaped like a long tube with fins.

easy.def: An important job someone is sent to do.
examples: The astronauts' mission is to go to space.
The dog's mission was to find the ball.
Our mission is to clean the park.

more.def: An important task that a person or group is sent to do.
examples: The mission of the spaceship was to explore Mars.
Our class has a mission to clean the park.
The rescue team completed its mission.

easy.def: Something that is wrong.
examples: I made a mistake.
There is a mistake in my math.
An eraser fixes a mistake.

more.def: An action or answer that is not right.
examples: She found one mistake in her spelling test.
It was a mistake to leave the door open.
Everybody makes mistakes when they are learning something new.

easy.def: A polite word before a man's name.
examples: Mister Lee is my teacher.
Hello, Mister Brown.
Thank you, Mister Jones.

more.def: A polite title used before a man's name.
examples: Mister Garcia teaches our music class.
Thank you, Mister Lee, for the ride.
Mister Brown waved from his porch.

easy.def: To get the wrong idea about something.
examples: I misunderstood the rules.
She misunderstood me.
We misunderstood the sign.

more.def: To fail to understand what someone says or means.
examples: I misunderstood the directions and went the wrong way.
She misunderstood what he said.
They misunderstood the sign.

easy.def: When you get the wrong idea about something.
examples: It was a misunderstanding.
We had a misunderstanding.
The misunderstanding was cleared up.

more.def: A mistake in understanding what someone says or means.
examples: It was only a misunderstanding, and we laughed.
A misunderstanding made us go to the wrong room.
They cleared up the misunderstanding with a talk.

easy.def: To stir things together.
examples: Mix the paint.
She mixed the batter.
He mixes the salad.

more.def: To stir or blend things together.
examples: Mix the flour and eggs in a bowl.
She mixed red and yellow paint to make orange.
He mixed the salad with a big spoon.

related.def: To mix again; a new mix of a song.
